subject: Under-stairs storage designed to fit
hook: The stairs set the angle. We build every panel to follow it.
ig:
The stairs set the angle. We build every panel to follow it.

No two staircases have quite the same rise, so under-stairs storage that genuinely fits cannot come off a shelf. Here is how we work through it:

Survey: we take heights at the tall and short ends, the depth and the slope, and note meters, cables and anything that needs to stay reachable.
Design: you see the layout before anything is cut, with tall bays where there is height and drawers or pull-outs where it drops away.
Workshop: panels are cut on our sliding table panel saw, edged on the edge bander and assembled in Hanley.
Fitting: our own team installs it and scribes the final fillers to your walls and floor.

The result is under-stairs storage that uses the whole space rather than the easy half.

Want to see the kind of pieces we make? Comment STAIRS and we will send you the link.
fb:
Ever wondered how a cupboard ends up matching the exact angle of your stairs?

This is how we work. It starts with a survey of the slope and anything tucked away under there, like the meter. The panels are then cut to that angle in our Hanley workshop, edged so no raw board shows, and assembled before they leave. Our own team fits them and scribes the last filler to your wall so it sits tight.

That is the difference between a unit that sits under the stairs and storage that belongs there.
